fields.name: tier
fields.description:
Used in the UI to show the Tier of unit

This is the general rule for approximating a unit tiers:
=IF([@[multiplayer_cost]]=0, - do nothing
IF([@[multiplayer_cost]] is less than 500, - unit tier 1,
IF([@[multiplayer_cost]] is less than 1000, - unit tier 2,
IF([@[multiplayer_cost]] is less than 1500, - unit tier 3,
IF([@[multiplayer_cost]] is less than 2000, - unit tier 4,
else - unit tier 5

Characters don't have tiers.

fields.name: scale
fields.description:
A multiplier that dictates the visual scale of an entity. i.e. Setting this to 2 will make your unit 200% bigger than the scale that the asset has been authored at.

If this variant is a rider of a War Beast macro entity, this multiplier will not have any effect. A rider's scale is set by the mount.

Note: This does not matter for Chariots, which use the rider scale independantly of the mount scale.

If this variant is a mount of a War Beast macro entity, set it to the scale that you wish the rider to be. Then adjust the value in the mount_scale column in order to multiply up to the value you want. i.e. If an Arachnarok Spider is scale 4, but has a character rider that is scale 1.15, set the scale to be 1.15, then the mount_scale to be 3.48 (in order to multiply back up to 4).

Sync Rider Cavalry variants must be configured to use an agreed-upon scale before animation begins, in order to avoid de-sycnchronisation.
